test_title: SSC CPO 2025 Official Paper (Held On 11 Dec, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: What is the trophy awarded to the overall champions of the National Games of India called?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Raja Bhalindra Singh Trophy**__.

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Raja Bhalindra Singh Trophy** is a prestigious award presented to the **overall champion team** at the **National Games of India**, determined by the highest count of **gold medals**.
 
• It is named in honor of **Raja Bhalindra Singh**, a former member of the **International Olympic Committee** and President of the **Indian Olympic Association (IOA)** from **1960 to 1975** and **1980 to 1984**.
 
• The **National Games** are the premier multi-sport event in India, organized by the **IOA** to promote sporting excellence across various disciplines at the national level.
 
• During the **37th National Games** held in **Goa** in **2023**, **Maharashtra** claimed the **Raja Bhalindra Singh Trophy** for the first time since **1994**, securing a total of **228 medals** (80 gold, 69 silver, and 79 bronze).
 
• Prior to Maharashtra's recent victory, the **Services Sports Control Board (SSCB)** had won the trophy for **four consecutive editions** (2007, 2011, 2015, and 2022).

 **Additional Information__**

 
• **Nehru Trophy**:
 
 
• Primarily refers to the **Nehru Trophy Boat Race** held in **Punnamada Lake**, **Kerala**.
 
• Instituted in **1952** to commemorate the visit of India's first Prime Minister, **Jawaharlal Nehru**.
 
 
 
• **Indira Gandhi Gold Cup**:
 
 
• An **international field hockey tournament** for women hosted in India.
 
• Established to provide Indian athletes with **global exposure** and competition against top-tier international teams.
 
 
 
• **Dhyan Chand Trophy**:
 
 
• Linked to the **Major Dhyan Chand Award**, which is India's highest award for **lifetime achievement** in sports.
 
• Named after the legendary hockey player **Major Dhyan Chand**, often called **The Wizard**, who won three Olympic gold medals (1928, 1932, and 1936).
